purpose: Separate boundary representation sensitivity from evaluation-length sensitivity in continuous-residual neural policy iteration.
status: Prespecified follow-up using previously inspected seeds; no independent-replication or runtime superiority claim.
primary_comparisons: frozen: step1000 minus step50 within each representation
frozen: relaxed minus full at step1000
iteration: relaxed minus full at step2000
multiplicity: Bonferroni across 24 primary seedwise comparisons (12 evaluation-length, 6 frozen-representation, 6 repeated-iteration); other steps descriptive.
interpretation: Frozen comparisons have exactly the same initial value function and frozen policy, using a fixed base plus an equally sized trainable correction. Repeated iteration starts both representations at the same terminal utility and retains Adam state between policy updates. Relaxing a boundary changes interior parameterization as well as trace restrictions. Neither comparison alone identifies a boundary-only causal effect. The 2000-step iteration is an early-budget test, not a replacement for the earlier 10000-step solver comparison.
